# Progress — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for progress when work is happening and the person is waiting: a file uploading, a build running, a form submitting. Show the number as well as the bar wherever you can, because a bar alone says roughly and waiting is easier when roughly becomes a figure. Indeterminate progress is the honest state when you genuinely do not know how much is left — a fake percentage is worse than admitting it. If the value is complete and meaningful at rest, that is a meter, not progress: progress is only meaningful while it moves.

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| ProgressRoot | The gauge. Owns the value and the range, and renders the track. |
| ProgressLabel | Names what is being done. |
| ProgressValue | Renders the figure beside the track, so waiting is easier with a number than with a length. |
| Progress | The namespace object: Root, Label and Value. |

## Native

### Features

Reach for progress when the wait has a measurable amount and showing it helps: an upload, a build, a multi-step task. It takes a value and a maximum and reports the proportion, which is the whole difference between it and the loaders — those describe a wait, this measures one. Prefer it over a spinner whenever the number is genuinely known, because an unmeasured wait shown as unmeasured makes people wait worse than they need to. Note it names its accessible name `accessibilityLabel`, where `LoadingIndicator` calls the same thing `label` — the two do not share a prop name despite doing the same job.
